title: Most news feeds are broken because they treat everyone the same.
body:
We have spent the last decade building algorithms that prioritize engagement above all else. The result is a feed that feels less like a window to the world and more like a mirror of our worst habits. It feeds us outrage and repetition because that is what keeps us scrolling.

But news should serve a different purpose. It should help us understand the world better, not just occupy our time. Truly personalised news does not mean trapping you in a bubble of opinions you already hold. It means respecting your intelligence and your time by filtering out the noise that does not matter to you.

Imagine a news experience that actually learns what you care about, whether that is climate policy, local tech startups, or global markets. It should surface deep analysis when you want it and quick summaries when you are busy. It is about curation that feels human, driven by technology that works for the reader instead of the advertiser.

We are building that at Headlinne. We believe the future of news is not about more content, but about better, more relevant content.
cta: You can see how we are rethinking the daily feed at HEADLINNE.com.
